newsitem.title: USA: Airports must speed cargo processing - Mergeglobal.
newsitem.headline: Airports must speed cargo processing - Mergeglobal.

text.p: Airports must work to help airlines and forwarders speed cargo through air terminals, an industry consultant told a meeting of air cargo and airport executives here Thursday.
"Most air freight moves at exactly zero miles per hour," David Hoppin, principal of air cargo consultants MergeGlobal, based in Arlington, Virginia, said.

"That is one critical thing airports can do over the next few years. That is help airlines make the ground process work faster," Hoppin told the 150 executives gathered at an air cargo symposium here.
The advantages for the premium paid to ship air cargo are lost if the cargo gets held up in customs clearance or moving through the airport to waiting trucks, Hoppin said.
Hoppin said the global air cargo industry moved 19.6 million tons in 1995 and that will jump to 31.1 million tons by 2001.
About 31 percent of the total is U.S. domestic traffic, 26 percent is between the United States and other countries, and 43 percent is outside the United States, Hoppin said.
Speed and reliability are reasons why the integrators such as Federal Express Corp and United Parcel Service " have grown so much over the last few years, he said.

"The integrators can offer a service reliability because fewer people are involved with the freight," he said. With traditional air freight, freight forwarders, customs brokers and others might be involved in the process.
Despite the integrators' rapid growth "we don't think the integrators will take over the world," Hoppin told the meeting. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 8982 Fax +5017
